title: Offer Acceptance to Week Four Activation Timeline
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, stepwise timeline and checklist from offer acceptance through end of week four. Designed for hiring managers, people-ops coordinators, assigned mentors, and IT provisioning teams. Goal: reduce first-30d time-to-impact and surface handoffs/contingencies early.

Scope:
Applies to: full-time engineering, product, and platform hires in NA/EU regions on standard onboarding. Excludes executive/contractor/air-gapped private-deploy customers (see separate playbooks). This is intentionally tactical — not an exhaustive policy doc.

Snapshot (one-line):
Day -1 to 0: acceptance confirmation, access gating, manager welcome note, seat & hardware order in flight.
Week 1: quiet bootcamp, focused access stabilization, 1:1s, environment first-commit tasks.
Weeks 2–4: growing ownership, syncs, milestone demos, role-specific skill signals.

Pre-Acceptance (people-ops tasks to kickoff immediately after verbal acceptance):
- Send official offer email and acceptance confirmation template (people-ops). Include: start date confirmation, relocation/remote stipend details, first-week agenda stub, who to expect outreach from (manager, buddy, IT).
- Trigger HR checklist: payroll forms, employment verification, benefits enrollment window (link).
- Intake to IT/Asset team: preferred hardware spec, VPN access tier, OS imaging, SSO group mapping. Mark as HIGH if hire is on-call or will access dedicated infra.
- Manager: confirm mentor (buddy) assignment and 30/60/90 expectations doc to be shared on day 1.

Day -3 to Day 0 (onboarding prep):
- People-ops: create calendar placeholders for day 1 orientation (90min), team intro+context (45min), and manager sync (30min).
- IT: pre-provision primary accounts (SSO, email, Slack), request temporary elevated access for first 48 hours if needed for infra setup.
- Facilities: if office-based, ensure badge, desk assignment, and desk kit (monitor, dongles) are reserved. If remote, confirm shipping ETA and tracking.
- Manager: send personal welcome note (template included below) with a 2-line primer on first-week goals and what to bring to the first sync.
- Mentor: send onboarding buddy checklist and first-day sync time.

Day 0 (first work day) — orientation and low-cognitive ramp:
- 09:00: People-ops orientation (90min): benefits overview, payroll, security baseline, code of conduct pointer, Slack channel join.
- 11:00: Manager welcome & role orientation (30-45min): concrete first-week deliverable (small, observable).
- 13:00: Team introductions (30min): short intros, 2 lines: role and how they will interact with the new hire.
- 15:00: Mentor pairing & environment check (60min): access confirmation (repo, infra, CI), run through local dev bootstrap doc (link).
- Day 0 checklist items (quick):
  - Confirm laptop received / imaging success / VPN connects.
  - Confirm SSO groups match role-based permissions.
  - Validate access to primary repos and test pipeline (example: run unit test suite smoke).
  - Add new hire to team calendar and recurring 1:1.

Week 1 (days 1–7): orient, stabilize, first small deliverable
- Focus: remove friction. Manager & mentor should triage every access/credential issue same-day.
- Week 1 recommended schedule (high level):
  - Daily mentor check-ins (15–30m) first three days, then every-other-day.
  - Manager 1:1 end of week (30m): review blockers, confirm first deliverable progress.
  - Hands-on task: ship a small non-blocking change (doc, test, small feature toggle) that validates repo->CI->deploy flow.
  - Security & compliance: complete rapid security checklist and required trainings by day 5.
- Signals of success to capture (week 1):
  - Completed dev bootstrap without unresolved infra tickets older than 24 hours.
  - First PR merged or first task completed with reviewer feedback.
  - Completed payroll and benefits enrollment forms.

Weeks 2–4: ownership growth and visibility
- Goals: expand context, own a small feature/bug, demonstrate collaboration across one cross-functional boundary.
- Manager actions: schedule a 30–45min 2-week sync focused on priorities and 30/60/90 update. Schedule 4-week demo slot on team calendar.
- Mentor: transition from day-to-day troubleshooting to weekly design/feedback sessions.
- People-ops check-in at week 3 (15min): pulse on benefits questions, relocation assistance follow-up (if relevant).
- Deliverables by end of week 4:
  - Ownership of a clearly scoped work item shipped or in final review.
  - Documented onboarding gaps (doc linked to team Kanban).
  - At least two cross-team review interactions recorded in PRs or meeting notes.

Handoffs and contingencies (common failure modes + mitigation):
- Hardware delayed > 5 business days: provide loaner and prioritize VPN-less access flows; escalate to facilities + hiring manager.
- Repo access blocked (SSO mapping): manager to request admin approval and add temporary collaborator from mentor. Track via JIRA INF-ACCESS.
- No mentor available: manager becomes temporary buddy and people-ops flags for immediate reassignment.

Interview evidence and acceptance alignment (how hiring decisions map to week 1 signals):
- Engineers: link back to rubric categories used during interview (design, coding proficiency, collaboration). Create a 1-pager that maps interview evidence to first 30d success criteria. Use this to calibrate manager expectations and reduce mismatch.
- Template excerpt for manager (to send day 0): one-paragraph mapping interview highlights -> first-week target.

Manager checklist (actions owner: hiring manager):
- Pre-start: review candidate interview evidence, set 30/60/90 visible doc, confirm mentor.
- Day 0: personal welcome note, schedule 1:1s, set clear first-week deliverable.
- Week 1: unblock access issues within 24h, ensure PR review bandwidth, pair on first task.
- Weeks 2–4: enable meaningful feedback loops, remove cross-team blockers.

Mentor (buddy) checklist (actions owner: mentor):
- Before start: review bootstrap doc, reserve 1hr/day for first 3 days.
- Day 0: host environment setup, run first smoke tests together.
- Week 1: daily short check-ins, guide first PR.
- Weeks 2–4: weekly design/feedback session, help draft 4-week demo.

People-ops checklist (actions owner: People Ops coordinator):
- Send offer + acceptance confirmation and logistics email.
- Book orientation, benefits briefing, and send security training links.
- Run week 3 pulse, collect onboarding feedback via short form (5 questions).

Templates (copy/paste-ready)
- Manager welcome note (short):
  Hi <Name>, thrilled you'll be joining on <start date> — quick plan: Day 0 intro, Day 1 small scaffolded task (small PR), end of week 1 sync to review blockers. I'm <Manager name>, reachable on Slack @. Your mentor will be <mentor name>.

- People-ops acceptance email snippet:
  Congratulations and welcome! Please find attached: new-hire checklist, start date confirmation, first-week agenda, and benefits enrollment links. Expect orientation invite from People Ops and a reachout from <manager name>.

- Escalation note (if access not resolved in 24h):
  Subject: Escalation: Access blockers for <Name> (X days)
  Body: We have unresolved access items: <list>. Requesting expedited SSO mapping and temporary collaborator access. Contact: <manager> / <mentor> / people-ops.

Onboarding success metrics (first 30d markers):
- Time-to-first-merge <= 10 calendar days for engineers (goal).
- Zero high-severity (>SLA-1) infra access tickets older than 24 hours.
- New-hire satisfaction pulse >= 7/10 at day 14.
- Manager confidence rating >= 7/10 at day 28.

Questions and unresolved items (notes to self / to triage):
- Should we formalize a loaner laptop inventory in the same JIRA project as facilities? (pro: single pane; con: capacity tagging).
- Do we need a different enriched onboarding flow for hires touching dedicated customer data (private deployments)? Cross-ref to private-deployments preboard security checklist.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Dev bootstrap doc: confluence link (PO-DEV-BOOTSTRAP).
- Interview evidence bundle (candidate packet): HR-KEY-<redacted>.
- First-week task examples: small README updates, test coverage additions, infra smoke test template.

Version notes: v0.1 (draft) — working doc intended to be edited by people-ops and hiring managers. Please add inline comments and tag people-ops for approvals.
